name: Weight of moving object
eng: Mass of something that moves.
svc: How much a case, order or customer has to carry while it travels through you — attached paperwork, evidence, forms, baggage, the size of the record being passed along.
kw: weight load paperwork attachments documents baggage burden case file size carry moving
pol: Improving this means the moving item carries less — fewer attachments, less paperwork travelling with the case.

name: Weight of stationary object
eng: Mass of something fixed in place.
svc: The standing load the organisation carries whether or not work is flowing — permanent records, archives, fixed overhead, estate, legacy systems that must be maintained.
kw: overhead fixed cost estate archive legacy standing burden infrastructure records
pol: Improving this means there is less standing load — less fixed overhead, estate or legacy to maintain.

name: Length of moving object
eng: Any linear dimension of a moving thing.
svc: How long the thing in motion is — the number of steps in the journey, pages in the form, questions in the script, days from request to answer, distance a courier covers.
kw: length steps journey pages questions script long process duration distance route
pol: Improving this means usually shorter — fewer steps, fewer pages, less distance. Be clear which direction you mean.

name: Length of stationary object
eng: Any linear dimension of a fixed thing.
svc: The span of fixed structures — the length of a queue lane or counter, the reporting chain, the size of a standing policy document, the reach of a fixed route.
kw: queue counter chain hierarchy policy length span fixed corridor
pol: Improving this means usually shorter — a shorter queue lane, a shorter reporting chain.

name: Area of moving object
eng: Surface or footprint of a moving thing.
svc: The surface a moving item occupies — screen real estate in a form, area of a document, ground covered by a mobile team, breadth of a single case.
kw: area surface screen form space coverage breadth footprint mobile territory
pol: Improving this means usually a smaller footprint for the item in motion.

name: Area of stationary object
eng: Surface or footprint of a fixed thing.
svc: Fixed footprint — floor space, branch square metreage, desks, the geographic territory a fixed site serves, shelf space.
kw: floor space branch office desks territory site premises footprint estate
pol: Improving this means usually less fixed floor space or territory.

name: Volume of moving object
eng: Cubic capacity of a moving thing.
svc: The bulk of what moves at once — batch size, shipment size, caseload a person carries, the volume of a release, size of a hand‑off.
kw: volume batch size shipment caseload load bulk release handover quantity moving
pol: Improving this means usually smaller batches and lighter caseloads — though sometimes you want bigger.

name: Volume of stationary object
eng: Cubic capacity of a fixed thing.
svc: Bulk held in place — stock on hand, work sitting in a queue, storage, the size of a backlog or waiting list.
kw: stock storage backlog waiting list inventory queue held wip volume
pol: Improving this means less is held in place — less stock, a shorter backlog, a smaller waiting list.

name: Speed
eng: Rate of a process or action.
svc: How fast things move — cycle time, response time, time to answer, throughput speed, speed of decision.
kw: speed fast cycle time response turnaround lead time quick throughput sla decision
pol: Improving this means it goes faster — shorter cycle time, quicker response.

name: Force
eng: Interaction that changes an object's condition.
svc: The push you have to apply to make something happen — escalation, chasing, incentives, enforcement, marketing pressure, managerial insistence.
kw: force push escalation chasing incentive enforcement pressure effort persuasion authority
pol: Improving this means usually less force is needed to make it happen — less chasing, less escalation.

name: Stress or pressure
eng: Force per unit area; tension.
svc: Pressure held inside the system — workload per person, demand against capacity, deadline stress, contractual or regulatory pressure.
kw: pressure stress workload demand capacity deadline strain burnout tension busy
pol: Improving this means there is less pressure in the system — lower workload, less deadline strain.

name: Shape
eng: External contours or form.
svc: The shape of the process or offering — the flow diagram, the layout of a branch or ward, the structure of a form, the shape of the customer journey.
kw: shape form layout structure flow design journey configuration arrangement
pol: Improving this means the process or journey is better shaped — not necessarily simpler.

name: Stability of the object's composition
eng: Integrity of the system; resistance to falling apart.
svc: How well the arrangement holds together — team and structure stability, policy drift, staff turnover, consistency of a standard over time.
kw: stability turnover drift consistency structure churn integrity standard holds together
pol: Improving this means the arrangement holds together better — less drift, less churn, more consistency over time.

name: Strength
eng: Resistance to breaking under load.
svc: How much load the system can take before something breaks — resilience under a demand spike, robustness of a contract, ability to absorb a shock.
kw: strength resilience robust capacity withstand shock spike breaking absorb tough
pol: Improving this means it withstands more before something breaks.

name: Duration of action of moving object
eng: Working life of a moving thing.
svc: How long a moving item stays good for — validity of a quote, freshness of a lead, shelf life of information, how long an in‑progress case stays usable before it goes stale.
kw: validity freshness shelf life expiry stale lead quote ageing duration lifespan
pol: Improving this means the item in motion stays usable longer before it goes stale.

name: Duration of action by stationary object
eng: Working life of a fixed thing.
svc: How long fixed elements keep working — the useful life of a policy, a system, a contract, a trained skill, a piece of equipment.
kw: lifespan longevity policy system contract skill durability useful life obsolescence
pol: Improving this means fixed elements stay useful for longer.

name: Temperature
eng: Thermal condition.
svc: The heat in the situation — emotional temperature of a conversation, urgency, conflict, escalation intensity, how ‘hot’ a complaint or a market is.
kw: temperature heat emotion anger urgency conflict intensity escalation tension mood hot
pol: Improving this means usually cooler — less heat, less conflict, less urgency.

name: Illumination intensity
eng: Light flux; brightness.
svc: How well‑lit the process is — visibility of status, transparency to customers and staff, dashboards, signage, whether people can see what is going on.
kw: visibility transparency clarity dashboard status signage see visible reporting light
pol: Improving this means it is better lit — more visible status, more transparency.

name: Use of energy by moving object
eng: Energy consumed by a moving thing.
svc: Effort burned by work in progress — staff effort per case, customer effort to get served, energy spent moving a job along.
kw: effort energy consumption cost per case customer effort work handling labour
pol: Improving this means less effort is burned per case, by staff and by the customer.

name: Use of energy by stationary object
eng: Energy consumed by a fixed thing.
svc: Standing effort that runs whether or not there is demand — always‑on systems, idle staffing, maintenance of dormant capability, cost of readiness.
kw: idle standby always on overhead readiness maintenance dormant fixed energy
pol: Improving this means there is less standing effort — less idle capacity, a lower cost of readiness.

name: Power
eng: Rate of doing work; work per unit time.
svc: How much work the system can push through per unit time — staffed capacity, processing power, the sheer horsepower available at peak.
kw: power capacity throughput horsepower staffing peak resource output rate
pol: Improving this means more work is pushed through per unit of time.

name: Loss of energy
eng: Energy that does no useful work.
svc: Wasted effort — rework, duplicated work, chasing, meetings that decide nothing, motion that produces no value.
kw: waste rework duplication chasing wasted effort futile meetings inefficiency lost work
pol: Improving this means there is less wasted effort — less rework, less duplication, less chasing.

name: Loss of substance
eng: Loss of material, parts or resources.
svc: Resource leaking out of the system — customer churn, abandoned applications, drop‑outs, no‑shows, spoilage, budget leakage, staff attrition.
kw: churn attrition drop out abandonment no show leakage loss wastage spoilage leaving
pol: Improving this means less leaks out — less churn, fewer drop‑outs, less wastage.

name: Loss of information
eng: Data or signal lost.
svc: Information that falls down the gaps — context lost at handover, undocumented knowledge, details the customer had to repeat, lost audit trail.
kw: information handover context knowledge repeat asking again audit trail lost data silo
pol: Improving this means less information is lost at handovers and between systems.

name: Loss of time
eng: Time spent that adds nothing.
svc: Time the work spends going nowhere — queueing, waiting for approval, delays between steps, idle time, dead time in the customer journey.
kw: delay waiting queue idle time lost approval wait bottleneck slow dead time
pol: Improving this means less time is lost — shorter waits, fewer delays, less idle time.

name: Quantity of substance
eng: Amount of material or resource used.
svc: The amount of resource consumed — headcount, hours, stock, budget, consumables, licences.
kw: resource headcount hours budget cost stock consumption amount quantity supplies
pol: Improving this means usually less is consumed — fewer hours, less budget, less stock.

name: Reliability
eng: Ability to perform as intended, every time.
svc: Doing it right first time, every time — consistency of outcome, dependability of a promise, error and defect rates.
kw: reliability consistency errors defects first time right dependable quality mistakes accuracy
pol: Improving this means it is more reliable — right first time, more often.

name: Measurement accuracy
eng: Closeness of a measurement to the true value.
svc: Whether your numbers are true — data quality, correctness of records, accuracy of forecasts and reported metrics.
kw: data quality accuracy measurement metrics reporting forecast correctness records true
pol: Improving this means measurement is more accurate and the data is better quality.

name: Manufacturing precision
eng: How closely the output matches the specification.
svc: How tightly delivery matches the standard — variance between people, sites and shifts; adherence to the agreed way of working.
kw: variance variation consistency standard adherence precision tolerance compliance drift between staff
pol: Improving this means consistency is tighter — less variance between people, sites and shifts.

name: External harm affecting the object
eng: Harmful factors acting on the system from outside.
svc: Things done to you — regulatory change, fraud, supplier failure, weather, demand shocks, cyber attack, media pressure.
kw: external risk regulation fraud supplier failure weather shock attack disruption outside threat
pol: Improving this means there is less harm from outside — less exposure to shocks, fraud, supplier failure.

name: Object-generated harmful factors
eng: Harm the system produces itself.
svc: Harm you create yourself — complaints, staff burnout, waste, unintended consequences of a policy, side effects of a target.
kw: complaints burnout side effects unintended consequence self inflicted harm waste damage perverse incentive
pol: Improving this means you cause less harm yourself — fewer complaints, less burnout, less waste.

name: Ease of manufacture
eng: How easy the thing is to make.
svc: How easy the service is to deliver — how hard it is for staff to execute, training burden, number of systems they must touch.
kw: ease of delivery staff training difficulty execute complexity for staff hard to do systems
pol: Improving this means it is easier to deliver — less difficult for staff to execute.

name: Ease of operation
eng: How easy the thing is to use.
svc: How easy it is for the customer or user — effort to self‑serve, clarity of instructions, friction in the journey, accessibility.
kw: usability customer experience ease of use friction self service accessibility simple intuitive
pol: Improving this means it is easier to use — less friction for the customer.

name: Ease of repair
eng: How easily faults are put right.
svc: How easily things get put right when they go wrong — service recovery, correcting an error, reversing a transaction, rolling back a change.
kw: recovery fix correction rollback complaint handling put right repair reverse remediation
pol: Improving this means it is easier to put right when it goes wrong.

name: Adaptability or versatility
eng: Ability to respond to changed conditions or serve many uses.
svc: Ability to cope with variety — personalisation, handling non‑standard cases, multi‑channel, flexing to a different market or regulation.
kw: flexibility adaptability variety personalisation exceptions bespoke channels versatile customisation
pol: Improving this means it copes with more variety — more flexible, more personalised.

name: Device complexity
eng: Number and variety of parts and interactions.
svc: How complicated the system is — number of steps, hand‑offs, systems, approvals, policies, exceptions and teams involved.
kw: complexity steps handoffs systems approvals policies exceptions complicated bureaucracy layers
pol: Improving this means there is less complexity — fewer steps, hand‑offs, systems and exceptions.

name: Difficulty of detecting and measuring
eng: How hard it is to monitor and control.
svc: How hard it is to see and steer the process — can you tell where a case is, spot a problem early, control what happens next?
kw: monitoring visibility control tracking detect early warning measure oversight status where is it
pol: Improving this means it is easier to see and steer — easier to track status and spot problems early.

name: Extent of automation
eng: How much happens without a person.
svc: How much runs itself — straight‑through processing, automated decisions, self‑service, robotic or rules‑based handling.
kw: automation automated straight through digital self service robotic rules manual touch
pol: Improving this means more of it runs without a person.

name: Productivity
eng: Useful output per unit time.
svc: Output per period — cases closed per person, patients seen per session, orders fulfilled per day, revenue per head.
kw: productivity output throughput cases per day efficiency per head volume completed performance
pol: Improving this means there is more output per period.
